finding: A single transparent enhancement implementation cannot be assumed across these players. Chromium, MPV, and PotPlayer expose distinct rendering/filter boundaries; the app needs per-backend adapters and capability reporting.

supportMatrix.available: WebGPU can import VideoFrame as an external texture and submit GPU processing.
supportMatrix.limitation: Win-Box must own the video presentation/compositing path; hardware support and zero-copy are not guaranteed.

supportMatrix.available: mpv gpu-next is based on libplacebo and supports custom shader hooks; libmpv render API can embed video rendering.
supportMatrix.limitation: GLSL hook syntax is explicitly unstable; render API requires graphics-context ownership and careful render-thread isolation.

supportMatrix.available: Official update history documents native pixel-shader and video-filter features.
supportMatrix.limitation: No public runtime API for Win-Box to inject/manage PotPlayer shader chains was identified in the official material reviewed. This is an evidence-based inference, not proof that no private/undocumented interface exists.

recommendation: Define a common plugin manifest and capability model, then implement separate Chromium WebGPU and MPV/libplacebo adapters. Treat PotPlayer as external/native filter guidance until a documented and tested control interface exists. Label only actual model inference as super-resolution; ordinary scaling/sharpening must be named accurately.
